images.caption: Dolphins at Chanonry Point. The dolphins are most active during the rising tide, often approaching remarkably close to the shoreline, providing spectators with exceptional viewing opportunities. The area is also frequented by other marine life, including harbour porpoises and both grey and harbour seals. Birdwatchers can enjoy sightings of various seabirds, such as terns and gulls, that inhabit the region. The surrounding flora includes coastal grasses and wildflowers, contributing to the area's natural beauty

description: This circular walk explores Chanonry Point on the Black Isle. The point is well known as one of the premier locations in Europe for observing bottlenose dolphins from the shore. The walk starts in Fortrose and heads along the beach to Chanonry Point where you'll find a lighthouse and some splendid coastal views. You'll then head towards Rosemarkie Bay passing close to the splendid Fairy Glen Falls. The route then follows woodland trails and country lanes back to Fortrose.
